summary: The bill amends the Animal Welfare Act to ban gambling on animal fighting ventures (including broadcasts), prohibit mailing or interstate transport of roosters, authorize citizen suits with up to $5,000 fines per violation, and allow seizure of property used in fights.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Animal Welfare Act to strengthen prohibitions and penalties related to animal fighting ventures involving roosters. It contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing federal appropriations or expenditures. Any enforcement costs would be incidental and minimal.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation addresses animal fighting and gambling; it has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration policy, border enforcement, visas, or protections for noncitizens.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or armed forces policy.
While the bill concerns animal welfare, it does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, emissions, or conservation of natural resources.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement benefits.
The bill does not address schools, federal education funding, school choice, or curriculum.
Although the short title references 'trafficking,' the text concerns only animal fighting ventures, not controlled substances or drug enforcement.

The bill expands criminal and civil enforcement tools for animal fighting offenses by adding a federal prohibition on gambling on such ventures, authorizing citizen suits with fines up to $5,000 per violation, permitting property seizure, and strengthening interstate transportation restrictions. These changes increase penalties and enforcement mechanisms rather than promoting rehabilitation or reducing sentences.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules beyond narrow animal-transport restrictions, or globalization.
The bill has no fiscal provisions that would affect deficits or debt reduction strategies.
No language concerning legal protections or restrictions based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
The legislation does not address foreign assistance programs or international aid.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, or voter ID requirements.
The bill contains no provisions on data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No references to worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
